e-3470.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
e-3470.worked_solution:
First, using the identity $1 + \cot^2 \theta = \csc^2 \theta,$ we rewrite the expression in the parentheses: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,(1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta )=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot {csc}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the fact that $\csc {\theta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin{\theta}},$ we can further simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot {csc}^{2}⁡\theta  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

e-3472.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
e-3472.worked_solution:
Note that we can simplify this expression by transforming the denominator into a form where we can apply a known trigonometric identity.

First, we multiply the numerator and the denominator of our expression by $\csc \theta + \cot \theta.$ This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity $\csc^2 \theta - \cot^2 \theta=1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{1} \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

e-3473.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using Various Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
e-3473.worked_solution:
First, we factor $\csc x$ from the first two terms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡x+\operatorname{csc}⁡x{cot}^{2}⁡x-{csc}^{3}⁡x & =\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)-{csc}^{3}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the cotangent-cosecant identity,

$$
1+ \cot^2 x=\csc^2 x ,
$$

we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)-{csc}^{3}⁡x & =\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot ({csc}^{2}⁡x)-{csc}^{3}⁡x \\  & ={csc}^{3}⁡x-{csc}^{3}⁡x \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-3497.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
e-3497.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following identity: 

$$
1= \csc^2{\theta} -\cot^2{\theta}
$$

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, and then factoring it as a difference of squares, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )\,\cancel{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}}{\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }}+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ we rewrite and simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}

decision.explanation: Combining terms gives (\csc^2\theta-\cot^2\theta)/\cot\theta. Since \csc^2\theta-\cot^2\theta=1, this equals 1/\cot\theta=\tan\theta.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
Using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
Using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡z={csc}^{2}⁡z,$ we rewrite and simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡z\,({cot}^{2}⁡z+1) & ={cos}^{2}⁡z\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡z \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡z\cdot {(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡z})}^{2} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡z\cdot \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡z} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡z}{{sin}^{2}⁡z} \\  & ={(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}{\operatorname{sin}⁡z})}^{2} \\  & ={cot}^{2}⁡z\end{aligned}

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
content.worked_solution:
Using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡z={csc}^{2}⁡z,$ we rewrite and simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡z\,({cot}^{2}⁡z+1) & ={cos}^{2}⁡z\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡z \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡z\cdot {(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡z})}^{2} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡z\cdot \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡z} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡z}{{sin}^{2}⁡z} \\  & ={(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}{\operatorname{sin}⁡z})}^{2} \\  & ={cot}^{2}⁡z\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ we rewrite and simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
First, we operate the first two terms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cot}^{2}⁡x}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x & =\frac{({cot}^{2}⁡x-{csc}^{2}⁡x)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{-({csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity ${csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-({csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x)}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x & =\frac{-1}{{csc}^{2}⁡x}+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =-{sin}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
First, we put both fractions over a common denominator and then subtract, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1} & =\frac{1\cdot (\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}-\frac{1\cdot (\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)}{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)-(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)}{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1} \\  & =\frac{2}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the identity ${csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1={cot}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1} & =\frac{2}{{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =2{tan}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}=2{tan}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
First, we write the given expression as:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -\frac{1}{{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor out ${tan}^{2}⁡\theta $ and use the identity 
${csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1={cot}^{2}⁡\theta .$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,({csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1) \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \,{cot}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Using \cot^2 x+1=\csc^2 x, the expression becomes \csc^4 x-2\csc^2 x+1=(\csc^2 x-1)^2=(\cot^2 x)^2=\cot^4 x.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $({cot}^{2}⁡x+1)^{2}-2{csc}^{2}⁡x+1?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the identities

$$
{cot}^{2}⁡x+1={csc}^{2}⁡x,\,{csc}^{2}⁡x-1={cot}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Then, we simplify our expression using the above identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({cot}^{2}⁡x+1)^{2}-2{csc}^{2}⁡x+1 & =({csc}^{2}⁡x)^{2}-2\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡x\cdot 1+{1}^{2} \\  & =({csc}^{2}⁡x-1)^{2} \\  & =({cot}^{2}⁡x)^{2} \\  & ={cot}^{4}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15

Which of the following is equivalent to (cot2⁡x+1)2−2csc2⁡x+1?

a
2cot⁡x+1
b
2cot4⁡x+1
c
1−cot⁡x
d
−cot2⁡x
e
cot4⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the identities cot2⁡x+1=csc2⁡x,csc2⁡x−1=cot2⁡x.

Then, we simplify our expression using the above identities, as follows: (cot2⁡x+1)2−2csc2⁡x+1=(csc2⁡x)2−2⋅csc2⁡x⋅1+12=(csc2⁡x−1)2=(cot2⁡x)2=cot4⁡x

First, let's recall the following identity:

cot2⁡θ=csc2⁡θ−1

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, and then factoring it as a difference of squares, we get

csc⁡θ+1cot2⁡θ=csc⁡θ+1csc2⁡θ−1=csc⁡θ+1(csc⁡θ+1)(csc⁡θ−1)=csc⁡θ+1(csc⁡θ+1)(csc⁡θ−1)=1csc⁡θ−1.

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
content.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the following identity: 

$$
{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, and then factoring it as a difference of squares, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}{{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}}{\cancel{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)}(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Multiplying the fraction by (\csc\theta+\cot\theta)/(\csc\theta+\cot\theta) gives (\csc\theta+\cot\theta)/(\csc^2\theta-\cot^2\theta)=\csc\theta+\cot\theta. Subtracting \csc\theta leaves \cot\theta.

after.name: Question 18
after.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the following identity: 

$$
1={csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, and then factoring it as a difference of squares, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}{\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }}-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta -\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
content.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the following identity: 

$$
1={csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, and then factoring it as a difference of squares, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}{\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }}-\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta -\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Factor the numerator as 2(\csc\theta-1) and use \cot^2\theta=(\csc\theta-1)(\csc\theta+1). Canceling the common factor gives 2/(\csc\theta+1).

after.name: Question 20
after.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the following identity: 

$$
{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, and then factoring it as a difference of squares, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -2}{{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{2(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)}{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1} \\  & =\frac{2(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)}{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)} \\  & =\frac{2\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}}{\cancel{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)}(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)} \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1}.\end{aligned}
$$
